items.front: Megasthenes — origin, sent by whom, to whom, account?
items.back: Greek; sent by Seleucus I to Chandragupta Maurya; wrote the Indica (describes Pataliputra & Mauryan society).

items.front: Fa-Hien — when, whose reign, what he noted?
items.back: Chinese, 399–414 CE; reign of Chandragupta II (Gupta); praised peaceful rule and absence of capital punishment.
items.examPoint: Fa-Hien → Chandragupta II → Buddhist practices in Gupta India

items.front: Hiuen-Tsang — reign, account, where he studied?
items.back: Chinese, 630–643 CE; reign of Harshavardhana; account = Si-Yu-Ki; studied at Nalanda.

items.front: I-Tsing — how he came, what he studied?
items.back: Chinese, 671–695 CE; came by sea via Southeast Asia; studied at Nalanda; wrote on Buddhist monastic practice.
items.examPoint: I-Tsing → India & Southeast Asia → Buddhist texts & sea routes

items.front: Ptolemy and Pliny — origin and works?
items.back: Ptolemy (Egypt/Greek, 2nd c. CE) — Geographia (ports/geography). Pliny the Elder (Rome, 1st c. CE) — Naturalis Historia (drain of gold).

items.front: What did Pliny the Elder lament about India trade?
items.back: The 'drain of gold' — Rome's gold flowed to India to pay for spices, pearls and textiles (in Naturalis Historia).
items.examPoint: Pliny the Elder → Rome → luxury trade & drain of gold

items.front: Ktesias — who was he and his significance?
items.back: Greek physician at the Persian (Achaemenid) court, 5th c. BCE; wrote Indica/Persica — the first (semi-mythical) Greek account of India.
items.examPoint: Ktesias → Persian court → first Greek account

items.front: Which two travellers are linked with Nalanda?
items.back: Hiuen-Tsang and I-Tsing — both studied at Nalanda in the 7th century CE.

items.front: Ma Huan — whom did he accompany, and when?
items.back: Chinese interpreter, 15th c. CE; sailed with Admiral Zheng He; documented coastal towns and maritime trade.
items.examPoint: Ma Huan → Zheng He → maritime trade

items.front: Chronological order of the core ancient travellers?
items.back: Ktesias (5C BCE) → Megasthenes (4C BCE) → Dionysius (2C BCE) → Pliny (1C CE) → Ptolemy (2C CE) → Fa-Hien (5C CE) → Hiuen-Tsang & I-Tsing (7C CE) → Ma Huan (15C CE).

items.front: The three Greek envoys to the Mauryas and their kings?
items.back: Megasthenes (Seleucus I) → Chandragupta Maurya; Deimachus (Antiochus I) → Bindusara; Dionysius (Ptolemy II) → Mauryan court.
items.examPoint: Greek envoys to the Mauryas — Megasthenes/Deimachus/Dionysius & account titles

items.front: Marco Polo — origin, when, whose court?
items.back: Venetian; c. 1292–1294 CE; visited the Pandya kingdom (Madurai); described the Coromandel pearl fishery.

items.front: Match accounts to authors: Indica, Geographia, Si-Yu-Ki, Naturalis Historia?
items.back: Indica–Megasthenes; Geographia–Ptolemy; Si-Yu-Ki–Hiuen-Tsang; Naturalis Historia–Pliny the Elder.

items.front: Why did foreign travellers come to India?
items.back: Trade (spices/textiles/gems) via the Silk Route, spreading Buddhism, diplomacy, and learning (philosophy/medicine/astronomy).
items.examPoint: Purpose of travel & the Silk Route
